papers.title: Medical multi-recall embedding: Adaptive retrieval for diverse evidence in medical RAG systems
papers.authors: Li C., Jing F., Li H., Dong Z., Xu Z., Zou H., Wang Q., He J., Qian Y., Cao B., Liu W., Qin S., Cheng W., Zhang H.
papers.abstract: Large language models have demonstrated promising capabilities in medical question answering but frequently generate unreliable or hallucinated content. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses this issue by incorporating external knowledge, yet its effectiveness critically depends on retrieval quality. Existing medical retrievers are typically trained under a restrictive one-to-one paradigm, where each query is paired with a single document, failing to reflect the complexity of real-world clinical scenarios that often require synthesizing information from multiple complementary sources. To address this limitation, we introduce a specialized multi-document medical retrieval dataset comprising 6273 queries paired with approximately 20,810 annotated passages spanning five clinical domains: general practice, cardiology, dermatology, breast tumor, and ophthalmology. Each query is associated with multiple clinically relevant documents that provide diverse yet complementary perspectives. Leveraging this dataset, we propose the Medical Multi-Recall Embedding (MMRE) model, which employs a one-to-many retrieval strategy enhanced by a novel Adaptive Multi-Recall Loss (AMR Loss). AMR Loss introduces three components–Adaptive Positive Margin, Difficulty-Aware Weighting, and Loss Normalization–and ablation studies on each component demonstrate that all three contribute effectively and work synergistically. Extensive retrieval experiments demonstrate that MMRE substantially outperforms competitive baselines across all evaluation metrics and domains. On average across five domains, MMRE achieves more than 10 percentage point gains in Recall@10 and significant improvements in Hit Rate, MRR@10, and NDCG@10. Furthermore, when integrated into a RAG pipeline with a frozen language model, MMRE considerably improves downstream clinical question answering accuracy by at least 4 percentage points across all specialties, underscoring its effectiveness in enhancing the factual reliability and clinical relevance of LLM-generated medical answers. The constructed dataset and source code are publicly availablehttps://github.com/WVKerl/Medical-one-to-many-data.

papers.title: The autonomy equation: How agentic AI reshapes trust and workload in routine productivity applications
papers.authors: Geninatti Cossatin A., Ferrero F., Ardissono L., Mauro N.
papers.abstract: User experience and trust in AI-assisted technologies are key factors in controlling their adoption. We investigate these aspects in an Agentic AI platform that integrates routine productivity services and exhibits different levels of autonomy: a manual baseline that lacks AI-driven automation, an Agentic AI with medium autonomy that requires user confirmation before acting, and an Agentic AI with high autonomy that acts proactively for low-stakes tasks. The study, involving 230 participants with heterogeneous professional backgrounds, examines how autonomy of the system affects user activity, user workload, perceived support, and trust.We found that both Agentic AI systems outperformed the baseline in user productivity. In task execution, they achieved a precision of over 82%, higher than the baseline’s 65%. The recall of the Agentic AI system with high autonomy was 63%. This denotes much higher throughput than the system without AI-driven automation (14%). The Agentic AI systems outperformed the baseline in workload reduction (NASA-TLX Aggregate score) with a statistically significant difference. Both AI-driven systems received equivalent or slightly higher trust than the baseline. However, the system with medium autonomy was the best at balancing productivity gains and user preferences for control. Specifically, the correlations between individual user characteristics (Desirability of Control and Propensity to Trust) and the resulting trust in the systems suggest that the influence of personal traits on system evaluation is least pronounced when automation is combined with explicit user intervention. These results encourage the adoption of user-controllable Agentic AI architectures in multitasking support.

papers.title: Multimodal fusion with LLM content via hierarchical progressive transformer for explainable fake news detection
papers.authors: Wang L., Li X., Zhou B., Zhang Y., Yuan J., Hu H.
papers.abstract: Detecting fake news on social media has become a significant challenge due to the rapid dissemination of misleading information. Current works often focus on combining limited modalities, lacking deep and progressive integration of diverse features. Apart from textual and image features, there remains a challenge in incorporating other features while also ensuring the explainability of the detection results. To address these problems, we propose a novel Explainable Fake News Detection method that integrates Multimodal Fusion with Large Language Model-generated content (LLM-MFEFND). This model utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate background knowledge and comments to integrate the LLM’s interpretation of news. To extract deep and cross-modal knowledge, we propose Hierarchical Progressive Transformer (HPT) to integrate images, texts, aligned multimodal features, background information, and user comments deeply and progressively. Furthermore, we design Multimodal Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (MLIME) method to provide explanations for the detection results. Through extensive experiments on datasets such as WeiBo21 (6,010 news items) and FineFake (15,140 news items), we demonstrate that the LLM-MFEFND model using DeepSeek outperforms existing methods. Specifically, our method achieves an accuracy of 94.5% on WeiBo21 and 81.1% on FineFake, representing improvements of at least 1.7% and 2.2% respectively over existing approaches. By combining LLM-driven context enrichment with robust multimodal fusion and explainability, our framework advances the fight against misinformation. The code is available at https://github.com/li1608335419/LLM-MFEFND.

papers.title: From exposure to followers: A stock-and-flow closed-loop framework of creator dynamics
papers.authors: Sun Y., Sun B.
papers.abstract: In the creator economy, platforms allocate exposure on feeds, and new followers arise largely from that exposure. What is missing is an estimable account-level closed-loop model that links platform-allocated post exposure to long-run follower accumulation. We develop an interpretable stock-and-flow framework with feedback: out-of-feed exposure increases with reach but saturates as the addressable audience is exhausted, unfolds over days after posting, converts into follower inflow, and is offset by proportional churn. The framework yields objects such as a viability threshold, a saturation level, and dynamic responses that separate timing from long-run levels, enabling diagnosis and planning. Using a panel of 1015 creators (794,051 account-days; 829,783 posts), we estimate the primitives via a low-dimensional pipeline and validate the implied dynamics in-sample and out-of-sample. On a strict 180-day holdout, the model attains a median MAPE of 0.020, comparable to strong forecasting baselines and econometric benchmarks. Subsample tests confirm portability across scales and platforms. By mapping traces to decision-relevant diagnostics of saturation, conversion, cadence, and churn, the framework supports design diagnostics and monitoring, and enables causal evaluations when exogenous variation is available.

papers.title: SRCR: Faithful structured reasoning with curriculum reinforcement learning for explainable question answering
papers.authors: Fan Y., Zhang H., Li R., Zhang G., Wang Y., Tan H., Wang Y., Li X., Liang J.
papers.abstract: Existing explainable question answering methods based on structured reasoning lack effective modeling of logical dependencies between steps and underutilize the potential of intermediate conclusions in structured reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose SRCR, a faithful Structured Reasoning method based on Curriculum Reinforcement learning. Specifically, we propose an easy-to-difficult reverse structured curriculum that gradually slides the initial state of reasoning from end to beginning, which fully captures the complex dependencies of multi-step reasoning. Moreover, we treat fact selection and deductive generation as a unified process and construct a faithfulness reward function to mine faithful reasoning steps during the model learning and exploring phases. Experimental results on the structured reasoning datasets EntailmentBank and STREET demonstrate that SRCR achieves state-of-the-art performance in factual accuracy and intermediate conclusion correctness, surpassing previous methods by 8.0% and 2.0%, respectively. Moreover, SRCR also improves answer accuracy by 2.6% to 8.3%, and extensive analysis shows that SRCR can generate more faithful structured explanations.

papers.title: FedDPKD: Federated learning with dual-phase knowledge distillation for label distribution skew
papers.authors: Shen F., Su W., Xu C., Liu Z., Feng J., He Y.
papers.abstract: The non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) nature of client data presents a major challenge in federated learning, particularly in the form of label distribution skew. This skew often exacerbates the tendency of models to forget minority and absent labels, resulting in classification outcomes biased toward majority labels. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach called Federated Learning with Dual-Phase Knowledge Distillation (FedDPKD). In this framework, client labels are dynamically categorized into majority, minority, and absent labels based on local label distribution. FedDPKD employs a dual-phase knowledge distillation strategy, consisting of Global-to-Client (G2C) and Client-to-Global (C2G) distillation stages, enhanced by a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism to improve training flexibility and efficiency. The proposed method enhances the global model’s classification accuracy and significantly alleviates the forgetting of minority and absent labels under label distribution skew. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, MNIST, and CINIC-10 demonstrate that FedDPKD consistently outperforms existing leading methods. Notably, under severe label distribution skew, FedDPKD achieves a 6.4% improvement in accuracy over the second-best baseline on the CIFAR-10 dataset.

papers.title: Instance and prototype contrastive learning for multi-view 3D model retrieval and classification
papers.authors: Zhou Y., Fang Z., Gu Z., Yang S., Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Unsupervised 3D model retrieval and classification have obtained much attention due to widespread applications. However, existing methods focus only on global representations while ignoring local saliency learning, leading to redundant distraction and insufficient complementarity. In addition, they neglect intra- and inter-class contextual relevance during representation learning, leading to inaccurate embedding space partitioning and missing representative prototypes. To address these challenges, we present Instance and Prototype Contrastive Learning (IPCL), an unsupervised dual-network framework that simultaneously captures view-level local features and model-level semantic information. Specifically, we treat each view as an instance and employ inter-instance contrastive learning to extract discriminative local salient features, mitigating redundancy and enhancing cross-view complementarity. For global semantic modeling, we establish class prototypes for 3D models and propagate the semantic information to global features via a prototype-aware contrastive loss, strengthening class-level discriminability. Innovatively, we employ a bottom-up adaptive clustering algorithm called voting clustering, which mines deeper semantic correlations to refine prototype selection and embedding space structure. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate the superiority of IPCL, e.g., IPCL outperforms most unsupervised methods, achieving classification accuracy improvements by 0.1% to 18.1% on ModelNet40 and 0.1% to 16.7% on ShapeNet55. IPCL achieves average retrieval gains of 15.2% in NN on ModelNet40 and 16.7% in mAP under the micro setting on ShapeNet55.

papers.title: Human cognitive process aligned rumor detection with small language models enhanced large language models
papers.authors: Zeng Y., Ding X., Cai B., Qin B., Liu T.
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of rumors underscores the critical need for effective detection methods. Recent studies have begun leveraging large language models (LLMs) for rumor detection in prompt-based scenarios Unfortunately, LLMs lack specialized skills without proper training in rumor detection compare to fine-tuned small language models (SLMs). To address these challenges, we introduce a human cognitive process into rumor detection to efficiently utilize data fragments. Further, we propose CoRuD, a multi-stage rumor detection method that integrates LLMs and SLMs, aligned with the human cognitive process. This approach integrates the strengths of SLMs in fine-tuned scenario and LLMs in prompt scenario. Specifically, it structures the rumor detection process into multiple stages aligned with the human cognitive process, generates expert insights through fine-tuned SLMs at each stage, and incorporates these insights into the prompts of foundation models to enhance their rumor detection ability. Our method achieves significant improvements across three public rumor detection datasets (Liar, Politifact, and Weibo, with over 14K test examples). It outperforms LLM-based approaches (e.g., surpassing GPT-3.5 by 17%) and various fine-tuned SLMs by over 5%, while also addressing the interpretability limitations of SLMs.

papers.title: Robust drug recommendation based on patient status awareness and unbiased prediction
papers.authors: Ma G.F., Wen X., Yang X.H., Zhou Y., Huang W., Li X.X., Jiang P.
papers.abstract: The AI-based drug recommendation system can recommend a suitable series of drugs for patients, which is a significant application in current healthcare field. However, current drug recommendation methods overlook personalized differences among patients, leading to the spread of personalized information among the generic patient populations, thereby resulting in information bias. Additionally, patients’ historical visits are not always strongly correlated, indicating that the patient may not always suffer from same or similar diseases in different visits. Therefore, we propose Robust Drug Recommendation Based on Patient Status Awareness and Unbiased Prediction (PAUP). First, we introduce a concept of the ”Standardized Doctor” module, which constrains the input and output of the model to capture patient-agnostic generic treatment strategies, thereby avoiding information bias caused by personalized patient differences. Then, we design a personalized patient information mining module that explicitly captures patient-specific information by mapping biases between generic and real drug representations. Through the two aforementioned modules, we formulates personalized treatment strategies for patients. Finally, we employ attention mechanisms to attenuate the influence of weakly correlated historical visits on current visit, which is utilized as auxiliary information to guide the final recommendation results. Additionally, we model both 2D and 3D molecular structures of drugs to preprocess drug representation. Experimental results on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV datasets demonstrate that PAUP outperforms the state-of-the-art in drug recommendation. In addition, compared to the suboptimal baseline, PAUP saves 59% of training time and 38% of inference time, with a faster convergence rate. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/PAUP-master.

papers.title: Clinical Data-Driven preliminary screening for Alzheimer’s disease via integrated imputation and evolutionary feature selection
papers.authors: Xu J., Kang H., Li H., Sun W., Sun G., Li J.
papers.abstract: As Alzheimer’s disease (AD) becomes increasingly prevalent, clinical data offers a cost-effective alternative to expensive neuroimaging for preliminary screening. This study develops a preliminary AD screening system utilizing clinical data with missing values, addressing the urgent need for accessible AD screening. In this system, we construct a framework that simultaneously performs missing value imputation and feature selection, overcoming limitations of traditional methods that sequentially perform imputation and feature selection, which neglect the complex interdependencies between imputation quality and feature relevance. Due to complex interactive relationships and the NP-hard nature of feature selection in medical data, we propose an improved genetic algorithm (IGA-G) that enhances standard genetic algorithms through two mechanisms: grey wolf optimizer-based exploration and dataset weight-based local search. The integrated framework couples multiple imputation by chained equations (MICE) with evolutionary feature selection, enabling robust analysis of incomplete medical records while maintaining computational efficiency. We analyzed 120 subjects from the OASIS-3 dataset across 222 clinical features. Experiments with four classifiers show that IGA-G outperforms seven algorithms across multiple metrics, achieving up to 78% accuracy with random forest and yielding an improvement of 2.3% over the best baseline. Ablation analysis further confirms the contribution of each component, and the integrated framework achieves a 3% improvement over traditional sequential approaches, providing a practical solution for community-based AD screening.

papers.title: A unified spatial-spectral pyramid mamba for hyperspectral image classification
papers.authors: Du P., Huo Y., Wang C., Zhang M., Wang H.
papers.abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification is vital in remote sensing for land cover mapping, environmental surveillance, and precision agriculture. However, achieving high accuracy with minimal samples is a major challenge. Mamba’s superior long-range modeling and linear complexity offer a promising solution. Furthermore, leveraging the 3D structure of HSIs, effective multiscale spatial-spectral feature extraction is key to improving performance. Towards this end, we propose the Pyramid-based Spatial-Spectral Mamba (PS<sup>2</sup>Mamba). It has a dual-branch architecture within a unified framework with three key modules. In the spectral branch, the Pyramid-based Spectral Mamba (PSpeM) incrementally captures hierarchical spectral representations through spatial neighborhood weighting and a bidirectional scanning strategy to enhance spectral discrimination. The spatial branch’s Pyramid-based Spatial Mamba (PSpaM) captures multi-scale, multi-directional spatial features, incorporating an innovative eight-direction scanning mechanism to encode both fine and coarse patterns. In addition, a Spatial-Spectral Interaction Fusion (SSIF) module enables efficient cross-domain interaction for seamless fusion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves overall accuracy (OA) scores of 90.90%, 95.62%, 93.09%, 95.78% and 91.83% on five benchmark HSI datasets, under a limited training regime with only 10 labeled samples per class. Notably, these results represent significant improvements over state-of-the-art algorithms, with relative gains of 1.20%, 1.11%, 2.61%, 1.14% and 1.87% respectively. papers.title: A self-modified hypergraph neural network for multimodal relation extraction
papers.authors: Xu M., Zhong H., Liu J., Song L., Li Y., Shi L.
papers.abstract: Multimodal Relation Extraction (MRE) aims to identify semantic relationships between entities in text-image pairs, playing a crucial role in multimodal understanding. Current graph-based MRE methods have achieved considerable success in modeling fine-grained multimodal interaction. However, there are limited by binary edges that require multi-hop reasoning and are prone to noise propagation. Moreover, these methods often overlook the exploitation of edge features, restricting structural optimization. To overcome these issues, we propose a Self-Modified Hypergraph Neural Network (SMHGNN). We construct a multimodal hypergraph where a hyperedge connects multiple nodes, enabling direct modeling of high-order semantic interactions. A key innovation is our mutually enhancing optimization mechanism between node features and hypergraph structure: hyperedges serve as feature carriers with attentional weighting, and the model iteratively self-modifies its connections through stacked HGNN layers to reduce noise and refine representations. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks show that SMHGNN achieves state-of-the-art performance, with a significant +1.84% F1 gain over the strongest baseline and a +3.13% improvement compared to the best graph-based method. The model also demonstrates strong robustness in low-resource scenarios.

papers.title: SageJavon: A scalable AI tutor for personalized programming learning
papers.authors: Zhao H., Wu Y., Lu Z., Yu X., Miao W., Chen L.
papers.abstract: Despite advancements in programming education, providing adaptive learning experiences while managing cognitive load remains a challenge. Inspired by Bloom’s Taxonomy, we propose the Learn-Practice-Evaluate-Support (LPES) framework, integrated into SageJavon, an AI-powered tutoring system based on Large Language Models (LLMs). SageJavon overcomes the limitations of traditional AI tutors, such as rigid content delivery and a lack of personalized feedback. It includes four innovations: (1) an enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model for personalized resource delivery, (2) heuristic and follow-up questions to guide problem-solving, (3) adaptive knowledge tracing and recommendation models, and (4) the FUPS-Score for automatic code assessment. Deployed in a 12-week course with 85 students, SageJavon facilitated 5306 interactions in the Knowledge Q&A module and 5144 in the Programming Mentor module, with LLM-based scoring yielding average scores of 87.39 and 84.19. Compared to traditional tools, SageJavon reduces cognitive load, showing improved scores in physical demand, temporal demand, and performance (all p < .001). It also improves constructivist learning outcomes, with higher scores in prior knowledge activation (5.01 vs. 4.78), knowledge transfer (5.09 vs. 4.82), and error correction (5.24 vs. 4.68). We compare our improved RAG with other implementations and find that it outperforms the others with a 2.93% average improvement. In exercise recommendations, we achieve over 80% user satisfaction. As the number of recommended exercises increases, both SageJavon scores ((Formula presented) ) and final exam scores ((Formula presented) ) improve, demonstrating the positive impact of personalized recommendations. These results highlight SageJavon as a scalable, plug-and-play solution for programming education.

papers.title: Feature structure co-optimized augmented network for graph anomaly detection
papers.authors: Zhang Y., Ma H., Bing R., Jia M., Wang X.
papers.abstract: Graph Anomaly Detection (GAD) aims to identify nodes that deviate from attribute or structural norms. Despite recent advances, redundant features and structural noise continue to obscure anomaly signals and bias node representations. We propose FSCAN (Feature-Structure Co-optimized Augmented Network), a plug-in module that jointly optimizes feature selection and graph refinement. FSCAN leverages spectral contribution-based selection, grounded in the Spiked Covariance Model and Singular Value Decomposition, to identify label-relevant features, while its adaptive refinement prunes noisy edges from head nodes and augments connections for tail nodes to enhance information propagation. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that FSCAN outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, on the Questions dataset, when integrated with a supervised backbone, FSCAN achieves a GMean of 67.35%, representing a 6.63% improvement over the best baseline; when integrated with an unsupervised backbone, the GMean reaches 22.49%, corresponding to a 10.98% improvement over the baseline. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/mala-tang/FSCAN.

papers.title: Source-free time series domain adaptation with class-aware temporal imputation
papers.authors: Zhong Y., Zhou W., Tao L.
papers.abstract: Source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) aims to adapt a pre-trained source model to the target domain without access to the source domain data. Recent time series SFDA works transfer temporal dynamics by employing a self-supervised temporal imputation approach designed to reconstruct masked sequences. However, this approach suffers from semantic ambiguity in the reconstructed input and task/classification-irrelevance in the reconstruction objective, which leads to the neglect of class-specific temporal details. As a result, the source model struggles to learn sufficiently discriminative temporal dynamics, limiting its performance on the target domain classification task. To address these issues, we propose Class-Aware Temporal Imputation (CATI), a novel time series SFDA method. CATI improves the existing temporal imputation approach during source pre-training by introducing a class-aware mechanism comprising two modules: Task-guided Contrastive Learning (TCL) and Gradient-based Semantic Enhancement (GSE). TCL refines the global semantic structure through contrastive learning to improve the semantic clarity of the reconstructed input, while GSE highlights local task-relevant regions through backpropagated gradients to guide the reconstruction process towards discriminative temporal details. By combining TCL and GSE, CATI enables the source model to better capture class-specific temporal dynamics, leading to improved adaptation performance on the target domain. Extensive experiments on four real-world time series datasets demonstrate that CATI surpasses state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods, with average gains of 1.41% in accuracy and 1.54% in MF1-score.

papers.title: Progressive feature refinement network for blind gaussian image denoising
papers.authors: Liu S., Cao L., Li Y.
papers.abstract: Robustly restoring visual information from images corrupted by blind Gaussian noise with unknown statistics remains a critical challenge in information processing. To address the limitations of static receptive fields in existing networks, we propose the Progressive Feature Refinement Network (PFRNet). Specifically, PFRNet incorporates the Parallel Expanded Receptive Field (PERF) module, which aggregates multi-scale contextual information via parallel dilated convolutions to enhance global structure perception. Complementing this, the Tri-Kernel Split-and-Fuse (TriSF) module leverages depthwise separable convolutions with heterogeneous kernel sizes and a unique split-and-fuse mechanism for adaptive and efficient feature extraction. Extensive experiments on five synthetic datasets and two real-world benchmarks demonstrate that PFRNet achieves superior performance while maintaining computational efficiency. For instance, with a compact model size of 7.86M parameters, PFRNet achieves PSNR of 26.55 dB on the BSD68 dataset and 29.96 dB on the McMaster dataset at the severe noise level of (Formula presented) .

papers.title: GAI-HIQ: Developing a health information quality assessment indicator system for generative artificial intelligence
papers.authors: Yi J., Du F., Nie Y., Liang W., Zhou X., Chen J., Li G., Liu M., Lv Y., Zhao W., Hou X.
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in healthcare has raised concerns about the quality of its outputs, yet existing health information assessment tools are not designed for AI-generated content. This study developed the GAI-HIQ assessment scale. Using Latent Dirichlet Allocation on 341 relevant publications, we initially identified three core dimensions and 15 secondary indicators for evaluating health information quality. A two-round Delphi consultation with 20 experts (100 % response rate) refined the framework to three core dimensions and 13 secondary indicators, achieving a statistically significant level of expert consensus (Kendall’s W = 0.288, P < 0.05). The analytic hierarchy process was then applied to calculate indicator weights, ensuring structured prioritization of quality dimensions (all judgment matrices yielded CR values below 0.1). The GAI-HIQ provides a consensus-based framework for evaluating health information generated by AI, offering practical tools for developers to optimize algorithms, for healthcare institutions to regulate applications, and for patients to assess information reliability.

papers.title: Bridging the gap in cross-domain graph anomaly detection: Enhanced source utilization and label accuracy
papers.authors: Yan C., Cheng X., Wu L., Xiao Y., Zhao H., Zheng W.
papers.abstract: Cross-domain graph anomaly detection is crucial for maintaining data security and system stability, as it can identify and respond to anomalous behaviors spanning various data domains. However, current methods are limited by their inability to fully leverage the complex source domain information and accurately assign labels due to the ambiguity and variability of anomalies across domains. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative approach, namely Bridging the Gap in Cross-Domain Anomaly Detection (BGAD). Our method employs high-frequency information-enriched node initialization and anomaly-aware denoised auto-encoders to deeply mine insights from the source domain and align them with the target domain. Additionally, a feedback-driven label shifting correction mechanism dynamically enhances label prediction precision. Our method has been rigorously tested on four different datasets. Compared with the most advanced CD-GAD method CDFS, BGAD has increased the AUC-ROC by 15.7%, significantly reducing false positives and false negatives, demonstrating outstanding effectiveness and practicality.

papers.title: A disentangled multimodal neural topic model
papers.authors: Xiong Y., Liu Y., Qian Y., Jiang Y., Chai Y., Ling H.
papers.abstract: This study focuses on multimodal topic modeling and attempts to separate public topics (shared across modalities) from private topics (unique to each modality) hidden in text and image data. To address this issue, we propose a novel Disentangled Multimodal Neural Topic Model (DMNTM). Specifically, we design the modality-specific encoder with an independence constraint to capture private topics, and the public encoder with a product-of-experts module to extract cross-modal shared topics. We conduct extensive experiments on six public datasets, including multimodal online reviews from Amazon, posts from Flickr, tweets from Twitter, and webpages from Wikipedia. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, we find that DMNTM significantly improves topic modeling performance in terms of perplexity, coherence, diversity, and topic quality over the best baseline. In two downstream tasks, including recommendation and sentiment classification, DMNTM further improves the performance. These results show that disentangling public and private topics effectively enhances both the quality and utility of multimodal representations.

papers.title: SR-DANet: Sparse-aware super-resolution network based on dynamic adaptive branch for medical image segmentation
papers.authors: Lu H., Kong D., Wei X., Xu X., Xu J.
papers.abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is critical for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, low-resolution images limit accurate segmentation of small or thin structures, and deeper encoder-decoder networks alone cannot overcome this sampling constraint. Super-resolution helps only when it is jointly modeled with segmentation in a task-aware way, so that the enhanced details truly support precise delineation of anatomically and clinically relevant regions. In addition, most existing deep learning methods fail to exploit the sparse characteristics of medical images. In such images, informative anatomical or pathological structures occupy only a small portion of the entire field, while large background areas contain limited diagnostic value. Conventional networks process all pixels or patches uniformly, resulting in redundant computation and suboptimal feature representation. To address these limitations, we propose SR-DANet, a sparse-aware super-resolution segmentation framework based on dynamic adaptive branch. SR-DANet consists of three key modules: mask generator, hash-based sparse attention mechanism and dynamic adaptive branch module. The mask generator identifies informative regions and guides selective feature refinement. The hash-based sparse attention mechanism restricts attention computation to relevant tokens, improving both accuracy and efficiency. And the dynamic adaptive branch module adjusts receptive fields across layers, enabling flexible feature extraction from fine details to global semantics. We evaluate SR-DANet on BraTS 2021 (1470 cases), BraTS-TCGA-LGG (65 cases), and MSD Colon Cancer (190 cases) datasets. Our method achieves Dice scores of 92.45%, 96.91%, and 93.63%, respectively, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines by 0.45% on average. These results demonstrate that SR-DANet effectively enhances segmentation accuracy and efficiency by leveraging the sparse nature of medical images.

papers.title: Exploring factors influencing open government data value realization in China: A mixed design using grounded theory, system dynamics, and questionnaire survey
papers.authors: Sun Y., Luan Z., Ma J.
papers.abstract: As digital economy strategies advance and the data market gradually matures, the pathways for realizing the value of China’s government open data have undergone significant changes, with numerous emerging influencing factors. Previous research has primarily relied on portal operational data and static efficiency assessment methods, making it challenging to identify the evolutionary mechanisms and dynamic relationships among these factors. To bridge this gap and inform policy-making and theoretical advancements, we employ a hybrid design that combines grounded theory and system dynamics. Utilizing 33 semi-structured interviews and 317 questionnaire responses (292 valid), we construct causal loops and a stock-flow structure. A 60-month simulation analysis examines factors influencing open government data (OGD) value realization, focusing on: (a) influencing factors and feedback positions; (b) the ranking of factor strengths and directionality. Our findings reveal that increased data demand rates sustainably elevate the long-run equilibrium level of government open data value realization, while higher data depreciation rates reduce this equilibrium. This research advances the dynamic theory of OGD value realization, broadens insights into key drivers and inhibitors, and provides methodological support for implementing strategies such as prioritizing high-demand data releases, optimizing APIs and data rights confirmation processes, and enhancing storage security by mitigating data depreciation. Our findings indicate that enhancing OGD value cannot be achieved solely by increased accessibility or platform capabilities. papers.title: Information bottleneck based graph structural learning for OOD generalization
papers.authors: Liu Y., Sun M., Zhang Y., Wang Y.
papers.abstract: Graph out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization aims to learn generalizable knowledge from source domains that can transfer to unseen target domains. Existing methods typically assume a single-source setting and rely heavily on supervised labels, which renders them inadequate for modeling complex distribution shifts across multi-source domains with heterogeneous feature spaces and limited labeled data. To this end, we propose the information bottleneck based graph structural learning method tailored for multi-source settings. The core insight is to mitigate the discrepancy of feature spaces across domains and extract domain-invariant signals through structural learning. Specifically, we first derive hierarchical raw features from the graph topology to construct a domain-agnostic representation space among diverse sources. Then, we introduce an unsupervised structural contrastive learning module optimized with a refined information bottleneck to capture invariant subgraph patterns shared in multi-source domains while suppressing spurious and domain-specific correlations. Extensive experiments on seven datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model, which achieves an average improvement of 9.9% in node classification and 7.5% in graph classification.

papers.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) in recruitment has rapidly advanced in areas such as resume evaluation, person-job matching, and recommendation. This study proposes the Topic-Oriented Suggestion Model (TOSM), a deep learning framework designed to suggest skill assessment keywords tailored to multi-round interviews. The framework comprises two modules: a Graph-based Topic Learning Module, which captures latent relationships between skills and their contextual dependencies through graph representation learning, and a Topic-specific Keyword Suggestion Module, which dynamically adapts attention to the thematic topic focus of each interview round. Using a real-world dataset of multi-round interview cases from a leading technology company, TOSM achieves superior performance compared with baseline methods in keyword suggestion tasks. Visualization analyses further demonstrate that the model components effectively bridge vocabulary mismatches across different recruitment texts and adjusts its focus according to each interview round. This study contributes by proposing a novel framework that integrates graph-based topic model with multi-label learning. It extends AI-assisted recruitment research to the domain of interviewer questioning. papers.title: Coal-gas risk fusion identification and warning based on deep explainable expert learning networks: A case study in mining information systems
papers.authors: Liu C., Wang E., Li Z., Xu J., Yin S.
papers.abstract: Reliable and interpretable systems for integrated identification and warning of gas hazards are essential for improving workers’ risk recognition and ensuring coal mine safety. Traditional statistical methods lack generalization and fail to capture multi-indicator coupling, whereas deep learning models, despite their accuracy, are limited by poor interpretability. The dataset used in this study was collected from 35 coal mines in Guizhou Province. By integrating field records, risk annotations, and feature analyses, a total of 22,460 samples were generated through a sliding-window approach, with a risk-to-non-risk ratio of approximately 35% to 65%. Based on this dataset and motivated by the aforementioned limitations, we propose a multi-source coal-gas risk fusion early warning method based on a deep-explainable hybrid learning expert network. Data distribution characteristics are adaptively pre-processed using boxplots and MICE, and representative indicators are selected through multi-angle correlation and precursor feature analysis. A one-dimensional multi-scale multi-attention parallel convolution network (MACN) is developed, and explainable risk modeling is achieved by integrating InterpGN with SBM. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 97.2% accuracy and 98.6% F1 score, surpassing conventional machine learning and deep learning baselines by 3.90% and 4.35%, respectively. Unlike post-hoc attribution methods such as SHAP, our model incorporates an endogenous explainable mechanism, marking the first application of such hybrid networks in the field of coal-gas disaster prevention. It provides a new paradigm for intelligent early warning expert information systems and scientific decision-making in coal mines. papers.abstract: Conventional two-stage hazy crowd counting suffers from error propagation between separate dehazing and counting pipelines, leading to degraded performance. To address this, we propose an end-to-end single-stage framework that jointly optimizes haze-invariant feature learning and crowd density estimation, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy through two key innovations. Frequency-embedded Hybrid Attention Aggregation (FHAA): This module uses frequency-domain attention to explore frequency features in hazy images, thereby enhancing key feature capture and improving feature learning. Experiments show it reduces Mean Absolute Error (MAE) by 34.48% compared to the model without it, proving its effectiveness in boosting performance. Haze-prior Guided Learning Mechanism: It explicitly models haze distortion, understands haze’s impact on images, and adaptively mitigates interference without manual dehazing annotations, reducing annotation cost and difficulty. Comparative experiments reveal a further 13.64% MAE reduction compared to the model without this mechanism, validating its anti-interference capability. The FHAA module focuses on key frequency features for crowd counting, suppressing haze noise and improving robustness in hazy weather. The haze-prior mechanism uses predicted haze distribution maps to adjust feature learning based on haze intensity, adapting to complex hazy scenes. To support research, we release two synthetic hazy crowd counting datasets athttps://github.com/312524/Hazy-CC-extended. These datasets, with the same scale as Hazy-ShanghaiTechRGBD but higher haze densities, address the lack of haze-intensity diversity in existing benchmarks. papers.abstract: Recently, Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) under uncertain missing modalities has become a critical challenge in the field of emotional computing. Although some effective models have been developed, these models largely fail to consider the influence of modalities’ quality on the multimodal fusion and missing modalities’ completion. To tackle these issues, we propose a Fusion Decomposition and Backbone Gathering based MSA model under uncertain missing modalities, FDBG, which includes four innovative works. (1) Inspired by the pyramid convolution structure, we devise a pyramid multi-head attention mechanism, which serves as an important calculation foundation for the feature learning in FDBG; (2) To improve the quality of each modality, we suggest a pyramid prior enhancement method that combines the current sample with several similar historical samples; (3) We put forward a fusion decomposition method to effectively complete the missing modalities, which first fuses the three modalities with the pyramid self-attention, and then decomposes the fusion feature into three modalities and completes the missing modalities with the self-attention interaction mechanism; and (4) To eliminate the interference, we introduce a backbone gathering method to translate and fuse the three modalities into a single modality. Based on three public benchmark datasets (IEMOCAP, MELD and CMU-MOSI), we conduct extensive experiments and prove that FDBG outperforms the 12 baseline models. papers.title: Dynamic loss balancing for long-tailed multi-label problem in document-level relation extraction
papers.authors: Zhang W., Xu M., Xu T.
papers.abstract: Documents contain multiple entity pairs, with specific pairs associated with multiple relations. The long-tailed distribution of relations further exacerbates the complexity of the document-level relation extraction (DocRE) task. In this study, we introduce a novel DocRE framework called HeterDLB. The HeterDLB constructs mention-level heterogeneous graphs by employing two types of meta-paths to capture the rich structural and contextual information within the document. To address the long-tailed distribution in multi-label DocRE, we propose an adaptive confidence threshold strategy that effectively distinguishes between positive and negative classes. To mitigate the imbalance between positive and negative classes during the training process, we first define the gradient update process of HeterDLB as a multi-objective optimization problem that involves adjusting the penalty strength among various loss functions through dynamic weights. We evaluate the HeterDLB on four benchmark datasets: DocRED, Re-DocRED, and two biomedical datasets, CDR and GDA. HeterDLB achieves F<inf>1</inf> scores of 65.96% and 82.20% on DocRED and Re-DocRED, and 70.95% and 85.18% on CDR and GDA, respectively. Compared to the recent models, HeterDLB achieves average F<inf>1</inf> score improvements of 5.43%, 15.48%, 4.07%, and 7.85% on the respective datasets when using the BERT<inf>base</inf> model. Extensive experiments from multiple perspectives further validate the effectiveness of our framework.

papers.title: Pontis: A decentralized framework for unifying remote attestation and enabling interoperability between heterogeneous TEEs
papers.authors: Li J., Lei H., Luo X., Zhang L., Shen P., Huang T., Cheng J.
papers.abstract: In modern decentralized information systems, establishing verifiable trust in remote computing environments has emerged as a critical challenge for secure cross-domain collaboration. Hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) such as Intel SGX and ARM TrustZone offer a promising foundation for addressing this challenge through cryptographically verifiable execution guarantees, but their incompatible Remote Attestation (RA) mechanisms create fundamental barriers to cross-platform trust establishment. Current solutions either focus on single-vendor ecosystems or introduce prohibitive architectural complexity, failing to address the critical need for lightweight, decentralized interoperability. This paper presents Pontis, a decentralized blockchain-based framework that solves unified RA and cross-platform communication challenges for heterogeneous TEEs through three key innovations: (1) a distributed off-chain Coordinator that normalizes vendor-specific attestation protocols, combined with blockchain-anchored decentralized identifiers that provide immutable distributed identities for TEE instances; (2) blockchain-based smart contracts implementing Registration, Attestation, and Management functions for immutable trust status propagation; and (3) secure cross-TEE communication channels built on the Noise protocol framework. Pontis reduces attestation complexity from O(n2) → O(n), achieving up to 99% reduction in required attestations for large-scale deployments. Comprehensive evaluations on heterogeneous TEE platforms, including Intel SGX and ARM TrustZone, demonstrate that Pontis maintains an attestation latency of 60 ms with over 10,000 TEE instances, while establishing a trusted channel between heterogeneous TEEs requires only 5 ms. These results demonstrate the robustness and feasibility of Pontis, establishing a robust foundation for secure, scalable, and flexible cross-platform collaboration in demanding heterogeneous computing environments.

papers.title: Ubuntu-IntAct: A dialogue-act annotated multi-party conversation dataset and graph-based intention modeling
papers.authors: Hu Z., Jiang C., Cui Y., Li R., Zhang W., Lin J.
papers.abstract: Multi-party dialogues involve multiple speakers, dynamic roles, and complex discourse structures, which pose significant challenges for dialogue modeling. Graph-based methods are a natural choice to capture such interactions, but current approaches often ignore speaker intentions and simply connect utterances as nodes, leading to oversimplified graph construction and low interpretability. To bridge this gap, we construct Ubuntu-IntAct, a large-scale dataset of 25,000 multi-party conversations, in which every utterance is annotated with one of eight dialogue acts (e.g., Query, Response, Suggestion). Building on this resource, we propose GraphInt, a graph-based model that explicitly incorporates dialogue acts as edge types to encode speaker intentions. Experiments show that GraphInt achieves substantial improvements over BART, including +17.7% BLEU-1 and +27.1% METEOR, demonstrating the effectiveness of intention-aware graph modeling for multi-party response generation. papers.title: Decoding inner speech via frequency-specific cortical EEG representations
papers.authors: Wang Y., Cai H., Zhou L., Yang Z., Wang L., Zhao J., Kuang Z., Wang H., Xu D.
papers.abstract: Neural decoding of inner speech provides a crucial pathway for silent communication and cognitive state recognition. However, existing circular brain electrical activity mapping (BEAM)-based decoding methods suffer from the problem that edge distortion and information loss easily occur, and they are mismatched with the input structure of convolutional networks, ultimately limiting decoding accuracy. To overcome this problem, this paper first proposed a frequency-specific rectangular BEAM sequence construction method that employed an adaptive variation function to generate high-fidelity EEG sequences across different frequency bands, preserving cortical spatial correlations while perfectly matching the rectangular input structure of convolutional networks. Then, based on the continuous temporal and multi-frequency features of rectangular BEAM maps, 3D continuous frequency-spatial and temporal-spatial dynamic representation modules, respectively, were constructed. Finally, a dual-branch 3D convolutional network was designed to achieve joint decoding of inner speech brain activity. The manuscript reorganized the publicly available InnerSpeech dataset, involving 10 subjects, 3 task modalities, and 4 categories, with the first 10 trials selected for each condition. In total, 1200 samples were used to evaluate the proposed model’s ability to accurately classify inner speech. Experimental results showed that the proposed method outperformed the baseline model EEGNet, achieving accuracies of 61.79%, 62.67%, and 53.25% in the Inner, Pron, and Vis classification tasks, respectively, while also providing new insights into the mechanisms of frequency–task coupling and the development of high-precision brain–computer interfaces.

papers.title: Structure-aware multi-view urban representation learning with coordinated fusion and alignment
papers.authors: Wei J., Wu S., Cheng S., Wang P., Lu F.
papers.abstract: Urban representation learning leverages heterogeneous data. While unified frameworks that combine feature fusion and contrastive learning have achieved promising results, two key challenges remain: 1) the lack of structural awareness often leads to suboptimal negative sampling and reduces the discriminability of embeddings; and 2) the inherently conflicting optimization objectives between fusion and contrastive modules may result in unstable training and suboptimal convergence. To address these issues, we propose SAMC, a Structure-Aware Multi-view representation learning framework with Coordinated fusion and alignment. SAMC introduces a multi-view contrastive learning module that incorporates structural similarity into negative sampling, thereby enhancing semantic coherence and cross-view consistency. To improve training stability, a flexible optimization strategy that incorporates soft Lagrangian constraints and stepwise state tracking is designed to coordinate gradient updates across fusion and alignment modules. Experiments on multiple urban datasets show that SAMC achieves average improvements of approximately 17.2%, 14.2%, and 5.9% compared to the state-of-the-art baselines on the tasks of regional popularity prediction, service demand prediction, and land use classification, respectively. Visualization analyses further confirm that SAMC enhances the discriminability, robustness, and generalizability of urban representations by embedding structural priors and adopting multi-stage coordinated optimization. Moreover, SAMC achieves a favorable trade-off between computational efficiency and predictive performance.

papers.title: Diffusion -driven group anomaly detection in spatiotemporal trajectories: Robust masked sequence imputation for enhanced pattern discovery
papers.authors: Ouyang Q., Chen H., Liu S., Li R., Wang K., Li Y.
papers.abstract: Detecting group anomalies in spatiotemporal trajectories is vital for smart city security but remains challenging due to noise and complex dynamics. Existing diffusion models often suffer from “conditional contamination,” where observed anomalies inadvertently guide reconstruction, masking the very deviations they aim to detect. To address this, we propose Diffusion-Driven Group Anomaly Detection (DGAD). Specifically, we introduce an Interleaved Window Masking Strategy that segments data to enforce mutual supervision and reveal latent patterns. We pair this with an Unconditional Imputation Mechanism that conditions generation on forward noise instead of partial observations. This prevents anomaly leakage and significantly widens the divergence between normal and abnormal behaviors. Furthermore, a Denoising Weighted Voting module aggregates outputs across diffusion steps to mitigate uncertainty and enhance stability. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that DGAD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, improving F1-score by 1.1% on average and 1.8% in high-noise conditions. papers.abstract: Rumor-refutation accounts on social media platforms serve as a critical means to address the issue of online rumors. But previous studies have neglected to evaluate the rumor-refutation effectiveness (RRE) of rumor-refutation accounts themselves. This paper proposes a novel multi-criteria evaluation method to evaluate rumor-refutation accounts’ RRE, namely the Optimal Clustering (OC)-TOPSIS-Sort-C method. The innovation of this method lies in its construction of RRE evaluation indicator system based on Social Network Analysis (SNA) principles and information credibility, trust propagation, and diffusion theory, and comprehensive determination of indicator weights by combining subjective and objective weights via game theory and Extended Fourier Amplitude Sensitivity Test (EFAST) method. Then, the TOPSIS-Sort-C method is optimized by determining the characteristic profiles between classifications using the OC algorithm of machine learning to solve subjective bias issue in the classification results, enhancing the automation and objectivity of the evaluation process. And the method is applied to evaluate 17,427 rumor-refutation articles and 141,259 comments posted by 42 rumor-refutation accounts on the Weibo platform in 2024. The results show that only 9.52% of the accounts exhibit fair RRE, while as high as 16.67% and 73.81% respectively demonstrate good and satisfactory, with the results aligning with reality. This method provides a new scientific tool for rumor-refutation accounts’ RRE evaluation and management, which has important theoretical and practical significance for the formulation of social media rumor-refutation measures. Overall, this study enriches the relevant literature on rumor-refutation accounts’ RRE evaluation and provides practical insights for other social media platforms.

papers.title: DF-NeRf: A geometrically consistent 3D reconstruction method for blurry images with decoupled and spatial fusion
papers.authors: Wang X., Yin Z., Zhang F.
papers.abstract: Reliable 3D scene understanding is fundamental to intelligent information systems, but motion blur in visual data often disrupts geometric consistency, making the reconstruction results unreliable. This paper proposes a novel blurred image NeRF framework named DF-NeRF, incorporating three core innovations. Firstly, the Multi-Scale Position Feature Fusion (MSPF) structure performs multi-scale feature fusion within the blurred kernel space to precisely estimate ray displacement ranges, thereby preserving multi-view geometric consistency. Secondly, the Multi-layer Independent Weight and Shifting Network (MIWS) is designed to achieve explicit decoupling between geometry and appearance. Within MIWS, the Dual-head Network (DHNet) employs a separate optimisation strategy, independently learning ray offsets (geometric attributes) and rendering weights (appearance attributes), effectively suppressing geometric distortions caused by motion blur. Meanwhile, the Prior-weighted Network (PWNet) employs prior-guided adaptive weighting to fuse different blur kernels, ensuring high-frequency detail geometric continuity. Finally, an edge-aware loss function is introduced to constrain gradient discrepancies in depth discontinuities, explicitly guaranteeing contour structure consistency and detail fidelity. We evaluated on public benchmarks, including 5 synthetic scenes and 10 real scenes, covering both indoor and outdoor environments. Experimental results demonstrate that DF-NeRF outperforms SOTA on PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics, with the most notable improvement in LPIPS. In synthetic scenes, DF-NeRF achieves an average LPIPS improvement of 14.32% over SOTA. In real-world scenes, DF-NeRF achieves an average LPIPS improvement of 19.79% over SOTA. DF-NeRF significantly enhances 3D reconstruction quality and robustness under blurred images, making it suitable for applications such as autonomous driving and robot vision. papers.title: HeterMV: Multi-view reasoning over source-aware heterogeneous evidence graph for multi-source fact verification
papers.authors: Gu J., Li W., Liu F., Liu W., Wang H.
papers.abstract: Multi-source fact verification aims to assess claim veracity using heterogeneous textual evidence. Existing methods lack explicit relation modeling for multi-source evidence. The framework unifies multi-source evidence into a Source-Aware Heterogeneous Evidence Graph. In this graph, core evidence, context, and reference documents are modeled as distinct node types. We then use directed multi-relational propagation to hierarchically aggregate auxiliary signals into the core evidence representation. Furthermore, building on this graph formulation, we construct four views to capture distinct evidence perspectives, including the multi-source fusion view, the core-corroboration view, the context-infusion view, and the knowledge-citation view. To tightly couple view-specific reasoning with claim verification, we introduce View-Conditioned Prompt Tuning to enable perspective-aware claim–evidence alignment. We further propose Cross-View Consistency Contrastive Learning. It uses the core-corroboration view as the anchor to align supportive auxiliary signals and suppress noise. Experiments on the Check-COVID (1,504 claims) and FEVEROUS-S (29,890 claims) datasets demonstrate that HeterMV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. papers.title: From answering to discussing: Advancing human-AI cognitive collaboration in dialogue agents
papers.authors: Li P., Wang J., Yang Q., Guo T., Liu Y., Wen Y.
papers.abstract: Current proactive dialogue agents primarily focus on gathering user information within predefined task schemas, but often lack deep collaboration mechanisms. While expected results have been achieved in well-defined scenarios, their shallow interaction patterns coupled with hasty task execution tend to prove inadequate when confronted with exploratory and continuously evolving personalized demands, confined to generic and non-targeted responses. To tackle this challenge, we define, for the first time, a novel Cognitive Collaboration Dialogue (CCD) task and propose its dedicated dialogue agent framework, CoCo-Agent. In such tasks, the AI agent collaborates with humans on exploratory, highly specialized, and personalized problems (e.g., personal career development), leveraging their respective cognitive capabilities to work together. Through trajectory planning, interaction coordination, timely monitoring and regulation, they gradually establish a shared understanding of the problem, thereby collaboratively developing personalized solutions. Building on this, we contribute CoCoDial, the first automatically generated multi-turn CCD dataset. It comprises 1460 complex dialogues across eight personalized domains with 120 distinct user profiles, featuring exceptional lexical diversity, fine-grained procedural annotations, and fully customized solutions. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that CoCo-Agent achieves state-of-the-art performance in collaboration quality and personalized problem-solving, surpassing existing baselines by an average of 58.4% and 3.8%, respectively. papers.title: Defending LLMs against jailbreak attacks through representation offset detection
papers.authors: Liu S., Cheng X., Zheng Z., Su S.
papers.abstract: Jailbreak attacks bypass the security mechanisms of Large Language Models (LLMs) by disguising harmful prompts, seriously threatening model security. Existing approaches mainly rely on pre-training on specific datasets, which are usually costly and time-consuming. In this paper, we propose Representation Offset Defense (ROD), a plug-and-play detection framework that requires no pre-training. ROD identifies jailbreak attacks by exploiting the representational space mismatch between user inputs and their actual intents, and consists of two modules: main intent extraction (MIE) for generalizing the proposed schema, and representation offset analysis (ROA) for quantifying the semantic bias. We evaluate ROD with six jailbreak attack strategies on two widely used LLMs (Vicuna-7B and Llama2-7B). papers.title: SMIR: Span-based multi-grained information refinement for joint multimodal entity-relation extraction
papers.authors: Sui X., Zhang Y., Zhao Y., Zhou B., Qian X., Guo W., Yuan X.
papers.abstract: Multimodal named entity recognition and multimodal relation extraction are two pivotal subtasks within multimodal knowledge graph construction. Traditional pipeline frameworks tackle the two tasks separately, neglecting the mutual support between them. Recently, word-pair relation tagging frameworks are proposed for joint multimodal entity-relation extraction (JMERE). However, these methods overlook the reciprocal comprehension among words within entities. To this end, we advocate focusing on spans rather than words to tackle this issue in JMERE. However, focusing on spans in JMERE is not trivial, which will encounter the challenges of information crudity and information redundancy. Consequently, in this paper, we propose a novel Span-based Multi-grained Information Refinement (SMIR) framework to address these challenges. Specifically, we first construct span representation matrices as a replacement for word-pair relation tagging. Then, we propose a multi-grained information refinement module to address the challenge of information crudity, encompassing global sample refinement, local vision refinement, and local span refinement, to provide more precise and comprehensive information for spans. Finally, to address the challenge of information redundancy, we design a span-guided cross-modality fusion method to integrate heterogeneous multimodal information related to spans. Experimental results on the JMERE dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our SMIR framework, which achieves 2.09% absolute improvement on the F1 score compared to state-of-the-art JMERE methods.

papers.title: RoleSimLLM: Towards large-scale and comprehensive social propagation simulation via role-based LLM-driven agents

Traditional rule-based agent-based models (ABMs) define user personality and interactions through manually crafted rules, leading to limited generalization. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer opportunities for realistic agent decision-making, simulating each user with an independent LLM is computationally prohibitive. Given that users of the same propagation role in social networks often exhibit similar behavioral traits, we propose a Role-driven Multi-agent Social Propagation Simulation Framework based on Large Language Models (RoleSimLLM), where each agent makes propagation decision based on shared role traits and its dynamic social context. Specifically, we utilize an LLM-driven role simulator to generate behavior distributions for each role rather than specific behaviors for each user, thereby reducing simulation overhead while preserving intra-role heterogeneity. A graph-based agent interaction module integrates these distributions with users’ dynamic neighborhoods to capture complex social interactions. This way, RoleSimLLM balances fine-grained user simulation with computational efficiency, enabling large-scale social propagation simulations. Experiments on million-scale Weibo and Twitter datasets demonstrate the model’s superiority. It achieves a 5.50% higher AUC for microscopic user behavior prediction and reduces MLSE for macroscopic propagation scale prediction by 3.66%, using only 1% of the computation time compared to other LLM-based methods. Furthermore, the model successfully replicates key social phenomena, including group polarization and echo chamber, through social simulation.

papers.title: Arbiter: Towards joint and fine-grained index and partition tuning in analytical databases
papers.authors: Liu F., Wei R., Wang H., Ding Z., Mo Z., Zhou K., Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Existing index and partition tuning methods optimize these components in isolation, leading to sub-optimal workload latency in analytical databases. We propose Arbiter, a joint optimization system that simultaneously tunes indexing and partitioning strategies through three key innovations: (i) partition-aware fine-grained indexing that creates dedicated index sets for each data partition based on local characteristics, (ii) a unified search framework that captures complex index-partition interdependencies, and (iii) query-driven search space pruning using workload-specific filtering and database-aware guidance models. We evaluate Arbiter on TPC-H, TPC-DS, and Wikimedia (ranging from 8.3GB to 100GB) across multiple workloads on Greenplum and DuckDB. Results demonstrate that Arbiter achieves up to 69.6% performance improvements over six competitive baseline methods while exhibiting the highest tuning efficiency through intelligent search space pruning. Our joint optimization approach consistently outperforms isolated tuning methods across all tested scenarios, validating the effectiveness of capturing index-partition interdependencies in analytical database optimization.

papers.title: CLER: A benchmark for Chinese litigation evidence reasoning
papers.authors: Bi S., Yu K., Li J., Wang X., Sun F., Miao Z., Wang J., Geng X., Wang L.
papers.abstract: Evidence prediction is the cornerstone of litigation, which requires complex legal reasoning to bridge the gap between facts and the parties’ assertions. However, most existing large language model (LLM) benchmarks do not offer a systematic assessment for evidence planning. Therefore, we introduce CLER, a large-scale Chinese Litigation Evidence Reasoning benchmark. CLER is built through a four-stage pipeline from millions of real civil and criminal judgments. The pipeline includes (1) semi-structured data collection, (2) LLM-based evidence extraction, (3) purpose refinement through decomposition into legal elements, and (4) validation through a tri-party adversarial review method that imitates courtroom debate. To this end, we obtain over 100,000 samples and conduct extensive experiments on 23 baselines, including open-weight, commercial, domain-specific LLMs and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. The findings indicate that the task poses a major challenge for current LLMs. RAG strategies, particularly a hybrid method retrieving similar cases, achieve the best performance with an F1 score of 54.4%, surpassing state-of-the-art proprietary models and improving the base model by at least 22%. Our analysis reveals several key insights. There is a significant performance gap with an average difference F1 of 16.2% exists between element checking in civil cases and narrative completeness in criminal cases. There is an inverted U-shaped correlation between case length and model performance, as insufficient or overloaded information leads to abandonment of precise reasoning, causing an average drop of approximately 10% in F1.

papers.title: API-DONet: A knowledge-guided deep neural operator network for flood forecasting
papers.authors: Zhang J., Feng J., Shao P., Liu Y., Hou A.
papers.abstract: Deep operator networks (DeepONets), capable of learning mappings between input and output function spaces via the operator approximation principle, have become a widely used method in Earth sciences applications. However, when applied to flood time series forecasting, DeepONets struggle to model the complex dynamic evolution of spatiotemporal features and lack explicit incorporation of physical principles, limiting physical consistency and predictive accuracy. To address this challenge, we propose an adaptive physics-informed DeepONet (API-DONet), a knowledge-guided neural operator network for accurate and adaptive flood forecasting. Specifically, we introduce a newly designed U-CBAM module as the branch net to encode the spatiotemporal relationships between different channels. Additionally, a decoder guided by the enhanced Fourier neural operator is used to extract global features, facilitating rapid and effective flood prediction under nonlinear dynamic conditions. Importantly, we design the loss function of the proposed model based on flood physics theory, ensuring that the predicted results are more consistent with the principles of flood physics. Moreover, we extend an adaptive gradient descent-based adversarial training strategy that dynamically balances the trade-off between prediction accuracy and physical consistency. Experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that API-DONet outperforms existing methods in prediction accuracy and consistency. Compared to benchmark models, RMSE and MAPE were reduced by 45.071% and 5.523%, respectively, while NSE and KGE increased by 5.182% and 22.058%, respectively. Code is available at https://github.com/KingslyZ/APIDNO.

papers.title: Human-in-the-loop learning to align cross-domain geographic knowledge graphs
papers.authors: Qiu Q., Zheng S., Tao L., Xie Z.
papers.abstract: Aligning geographic knowledge graphs is crucial for integrating multi-source geographic data and building high-quality knowledge graphs. Current research faces challenges such as limited datasets, reliance on labeled data, and poor model interpretability. To address these issues, we proposed a human-in-the-loop (HITL), learning-enhanced, cross-domain geographic knowledge graph alignment framework. First, it employs a graph attention mechanism to aggregate multi-hop neighborhood information and utilizes clustering to generate candidate entity pairs, thereby enhancing the quality of alignment sample generation through human-machine collaboration. Second, by integrating active learning techniques, it designs an uncertainty measurement approach based on ranking and distance information, enabling the model to achieve efficient and accurate knowledge graph alignment even with a limited amount of manually labeled data. Experiments conducted on our self-constructed geographic dataset, GeoEA2024, demonstrate that the proposed sample generation method can construct a high-quality alignment dataset while reducing annotation costs by approximately 98 %. Compared with mainstream alignment models, our approach effectively corrects misaligned samples produced by other models and achieves superior performance across multiple evaluation metrics, with the Hits@1 score improving by >4 %. Furthermore, the framework requires only a small amount of manual labeling to achieve performance comparable to fully supervised models after several iterations, significantly reducing human annotation costs and validating the efficiency and scalability of the proposed method.

papers.title: DUIC: User-descriptive intention guided clustering for personalized and understandable document partitions
papers.authors: Xue J., Huang R., Bai R., Qin Y., Chen Y., Lin C.
papers.abstract: Personalized document clustering often fails to directly utilize user-descriptive intentions expressed in natural language and produces clusters that are difficult to understand. We propose Descriptive-Intention-Guided Understandable Clustering (DUIC), an end-to-end model that integrates a Personalized Intention-Guided Clustering (PIGC) module with a User-Aligned Cluster Explanation (UACE) module. PIGC parses and leverages user-descriptive intentions to guide clustering, while UACE generates human-understandable explanations aligned with these intentions. DUIC was evaluated on six benchmark datasets (737-6,000 text documents) including MIND-6K, BBCSport, and ArXiv variants, against ten state-of-the-art baselines. It achieved up to 99.05% accuracy, 92.80% NMI, and 96.24% ARI. Compared with the strongest baseline on each dataset, DUIC achieved maximum improvements of 16.28% in ACC and 10.93% in NMI. Results show DUIC not only effectively guides clustering results to match user intention but also helps users understand what each cluster represents, bridging the gap between user-descriptive intention and personalized, understandable clustering results.

papers.title: Game-theoretic approach on strategizing cooperation model in community group-buying
papers.authors: Shu L., Zhou Y., Qin Y.
papers.abstract: Sound operational strategies and strong partnerships derive the development of community group-buying platform. Although the existing literature has concerned this unique platform, it largely neglects the design of its cooperation model. To fill this gap, this study proposes a cooperation framework based on a Stackelberg game approach in the context of community group-buying. Our model results demonstrate that collaborating with the local dealer through resale model enhances the platform’s profitability. Meanwhile, adopting a proportional commission model with the community leader can create a win-win-win situation involving the platform, the local dealer, and the community leader. Furthermore, a proportional commission structure exhibits superior incentive effects compared to a fixed commission structure in motivating community leader’s service efforts, especially when the local dealer operates in the resale model. Notably, our findings reveal that certain key parameters significantly influence the behavior of the platform’s partners, encouraging the local dealer and the community leader to adopt higher prices and exert greater effort in community group-buying service, while simultaneously providing opportunity for free-riding behavior. Experimental results confirm that the game-theoretic approach enables the platform to identify the optimal cooperation model, thereby achieving profit maximization.

papers.title: Functional data clustering and outlier identification via subgroup analysis with minimum spanning tree
papers.authors: Liu C., Lin S., Li J.
papers.abstract: Functional data clustering with outliers poses critical challenges in cluster number selection consistency, computational efficiency, and robustness to contamination. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel functional data subgroup clustering algorithm based on minimum spanning tree (FDSC-MST) method. Specifically, FDSC-MST constructs a minimum spanning tree (MST) using both geographical distance and functional curve similarity, then applies subgroup pairwise penalties only to MST edges. An alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is utilized to solve the optimization problem. For contaminated data, we further propose an effective functional data subgroup clustering and outlier detection algorithm via minimum spanning tree (FDSCOD-MST), which simultaneously performs clustering and outlier detection while enhancing robustness and retaining computational efficiency. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that FDSC-MST outperforms existing methods in cluster number selection consistency and clustering accuracy, even under outlier contamination. When compared to state-of-the-art methods with consistent cluster number selection, the proposed FDSC-MST requires only 17% of the computational time when the sample size is 200, with time savings becoming more significant as sample size grows. Validation on two real-world datasets (bike sharing system data and travel trajectory data) further confirms the practical effectiveness of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Beyond traditional search: New characteristics of online health information seeking about chronic disease with Gen AI
papers.authors: Tang Z., Su Y., Hansen P., Zhang P.
papers.abstract: Chronic health information seeking is vital for patient well-being and self-management, yet how AI aids this process remains unclear. To explore how users interact with Gen AI tools when seeking and evaluating chronic health information, this study conducted an experiment involving 60 participants, collecting 757 user-generated dialogues related to three chronic conditions. We developed a complementary coding framework integrating analysis of user behavior and AI’s response to understand user-AI interactions and their impact on chronic disease information seeking, evaluation and adoption. The results show that while user interactions with Gen AI share similarities with traditional searches, they also exhibit distinct characteristics: 1) User-input prompts are more detailed, with longer sentences and more terms to specify information needs. Users also adopt more diverse reformulation strategies, often informed or inspired by AI feedback. 2) Some users communicate with AI as if interacting with a human, and the AI often responds with emotionally supportive, human-like replies. 3) Users spend less time but engage in more conversation turns, as the AI provides clear, well-structured responses that maintain dialogue flow and adapt to user intent, thereby enhancing retrieval efficiency and encouraging continued interaction. 4) While most users evaluate AI-generated content heuristically and rarely seek external verification, encountering factual inaccuracies or low-credibility responses can reduce their willingness to adopt the AI's output. These findings offer a more holistic understanding of human-AI interaction in online health information seeking and provide valuable guidance for optimizing system design, enhancing algorithm literacy, and improving health management practices.
